# Mint Records

Notes from reading the published US Mint production ledgers and the
National Archives record groups that cover them.

The ledgers are generally reliable for the 20th century, though
reconciliation against assay commission records sometimes turns up
discrepancies of a few hundred pieces.

For the 1933 double eagle, the mint ledgers record 312,000 pieces
struck before the gold recall halted production. Nearly all went to the
melting pots in 1934, which is why surviving examples are so notorious.

Earlier records are patchier: pre-1840 branch mint figures often
survive only in correspondence, and several early dollar mintages are
estimates rather than ledger entries.

Related: [[1933 Double Eagle]], [[US Mint History]].
